# Design — keep speclaw's regenerable content local

## Approach

One gitignore edit, plus a detection helper, plus the dogfood application to
this repo. Deliberately narrow: only `ai-specs/` is ignored — the agent IDE
directories are left alone.

### 1. Gitignore `ai-specs/` in `scaffold()`

`src/modules/foundation/scaffold.ts` already calls `ensureGitignore` for
`.speclaw/` and `*.bak`. Add one line next to those:

```ts
ensureGitignore(
  projectPath,
  "ai-specs/",
  "speclaw workflow content (regenerated by init/update; never commit)",
  report,
);
```

`scaffold()` is the single chokepoint — `runInit` and `applyProjectMigrations`
(update) both call it — so this covers "al inicializar" and "ya instalado" at
once. `ensureGitignore` is already idempotent (it skips when the trimmed entry
is present), satisfying the no-duplicate requirement.

### 2. Leave the IDE directories alone

`configureAgent` (`src/shared/agents.ts`) still creates the symlinks
(`.claude/skills -> ../ai-specs/skills`, …) exactly as before, and adds **no**
`.gitignore` entry for them. Whether `.claude/`, `.cursor/`, etc. are committed
is the user's decision — many projects already keep their own skills/commands
there. A user with a real `.claude/skills` directory is unaffected:
`configureAgent` already skips creating a symlink when the path exists.

### 3. Detect and report an already-tracked `ai-specs`

`src/shared/git.ts` (new) exposes `isGitRepo` and `listTrackedPaths` (via
`spawnSync('git', ['ls-files', …])`, guarded so a missing git / non-repo
returns empty). `src/cli/lib/untrack.ts`'s `reportTrackedLocalContent` calls
`listTrackedPaths(projectPath, ["ai-specs"])` and, when `ai-specs/` is still
tracked, prints:

```
git rm -r --cached ai-specs
git commit -m "chore: stop tracking speclaw local content"
```

`runInit` and `applyProjectMigrations` call it after `scaffold()`. speclaw only
prints; the user runs it (Rule 6 — no git-index writes on the user's behalf).

### 4. Dogfood this repo

Add `ai-specs/` to this repo's `.gitignore` and untrack the tracked `ai-specs/`
files with `git rm -r --cached ai-specs`. The authored source is in
`src/modules/*/assets/`, so the generated copy is safe to untrack. This repo's
`.claude/*` symlinks stay committed (consistent with leaving IDE dirs to the
user).

## Alternatives weighed

- **Also gitignore the IDE symlink subpaths (`.claude/skills`, …).** An earlier
  cut of this change did exactly that. Rejected: it would stop users who keep
  their own skills/commands under `.claude`/`.cursor` from committing them.
  Ignoring only `ai-specs/` achieves the goal (speclaw's regenerable content
  stays out of git) without dictating the IDE directories' tracking.
- **Reuse `project-update` capability.** It already owns a `.gitignore`
  requirement (`*.bak`). Rejected as the home: this behavior fires on `init`
  too and is about git-tracking ownership of *installed content*, not the update
  delivery flow. A dedicated `local-content` capability states the model once
  for both entry points.
- **Auto-run `git rm --cached` during update.** More convenient, but writes to
  the git index without explicit authorization — contradicts Rule 6. Rejected in
  favor of printed instructions (the user's chosen option).
- **Keep the manifest committed** (`ai-specs/*` + `!ai-specs/.speclaw.json`).
  Rejected: mixes local content with one tracked file (fragile), and the
  manifest is regenerated locally on each init anyway. One `ai-specs/` rule is
  simpler and coherent.

## Trade-offs

The accepted cost: a fresh clone no longer has `ai-specs/`, so `.claude/skills`
resolves only after someone runs `speclaw init` / `speclaw update` (which
regenerate `ai-specs/`). This reframes speclaw's own workflow content as an
installed dependency, and is documented in the `init` handoff / README so
teammates know the post-clone step. In exchange: no per-`update` git churn from
the managed-file refresh, and no duplication of package content in every
consuming repo — while each project keeps full control over its own
`.claude`/`.cursor` content.
